_doc: Req 74419202 (#4452) — the WRITE-path half in `FileSystemVaultAdapter.replaceFrontmatter`: decision 1 (replace whole, normalise no line endings) and decision 2 (write back EXACTLY ONE U+FEFF). Both branches of the method have their own mutant, because B19/B20 replace an existing block while B25 inserts into a block-less file.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/cli/src/adapters/FileSystemVaultAdapter.ts

Q4_write_path_carries_the_whole_bom_run.from:
const leadingBom = existing.blockStart > 0 ? "\uFEFF" : "";
      return leadingBom + block + content.slice(existing.blockEnd);
Q4_write_path_carries_the_whole_bom_run._note: The pre-#4452 splice, verbatim: it carried `content.slice(0, blockStart)` across, i.e. ALL N bytes. Reverts decision 2 for the replace branch while leaving the read path fully widened — so only the «exactly one BOM survives a write» axis can see it, and the axes that merely READ an N-BOM file stay green.

Q5_no_block_branch_counts_at_most_one_bo.to:
const bom = content.charCodeAt(0) === 0xfeff ? 1 : 0;
    return content.slice(0, bom) + `${block}\n` + content.slice(bom);
Q5_no_block_branch_counts_at_most_one_bo._note: Same revert for the OTHER branch (insert into a block-less file): the surplus bytes would be left stranded after the inserted block. Narrow by construction — only an axis that writes to a block-less N-BOM file reaches this line.
